outcome: Full feature parity is not achieved or verified. Code presence, native placeholders/substitutions, unreachable branches and missing behavior are distinguished below.

scope_policy.include: Anonymous public browse/search/recommendations/lists/comments, local library/history/settings, lawfully returned media and downloads.
scope_policy.exclude: Accounts, login, registration, subscriptions, payments, account-dependent posting/ratings and private server lists.
scope_policy.authorization: Do not add synthetic subscription gates; honor actual upstream auth/DRM denials.
scope_policy.sensitive_values: No credential or shared-client-key values are included. File paths and line ranges replace raw source excerpts.

methodology: Read implementation rather than crediting function names/API wrappers as full user-facing behavior.
Every original inventory ID has one review row; scope and counts reconciled programmatically against both inventories.
Evidence contains precise existing paths and valid line ranges, no source literals or secret values.
No compiler, test runner or live API call was launched. Existing logs are historical/supplied evidence only.
Native behavior remains unverified even where plugin calls and Kotlin handlers exist. Cast/WebView/service gaps are not described merely as untested implementations.
Source hashes were checked after inspection; no lib file changed between the captured hash snapshot and report assembly.

status_definitions.code_present_static_only: Wired implementation found by source inspection. Not an assertion of executed, device-tested or complete cross-platform parity.
status_definitions.code_present_native_unverified: Wired native/plugin implementation found. Native/device success, permissions, lifecycle and files/streams were not exercised.
status_definitions.partial_static_only: Some behavior exists, but explicit original/target behavior is missing, substituted or known defective.
status_definitions.not_implemented: No implementation found, or feature is explicitly rejected. Nearby generic functionality is not counted as equivalent.
status_definitions.api_or_widget_only_unreachable: API/widget code exists but an important required option or branch has no reachable user entry point.
status_definitions.blocked_by_logic_defect: User-facing implementation is blocked by a definite static logic defect; no successful runtime parity claimed.
status_definitions.policy_divergence_pending_decision: Feature remains in original in-scope inventory but conflicts with present ad-free product posture; explicit policy/scope decision required.
status_definitions.excluded_by_user: Explicitly excluded historical feature; not a parity deficit or implementation credit.

defects.title: Initial player open overwrites persisted resume/history before reading it
defects.description: Player creation is followed by _open. _open first awaits _save, while initial _position/_duration are zero and _source/_episode already identify the selected item. _save passes those zeros to recordWatch, which replaces the exact title/episode entry. Only after that write does _open query history to calculate start. Reopening an existing title therefore destroys its prior resume position before it is used; even a failed initial media open can erase previous progress.
defects.recommended_correction: Separate first-open/resume lookup from saving the previously opened stream. Save only initialized/observed playback state, capture history before overwriting it, and add integration tests for reopen, failed initial open, completed reset, quality switch and next episode.

defects.title: Local identity is numeric ID only across poster and channel namespaces
defects.description: Watchlist membership/removal, collection membership/import validation and history replacement use ID (and optional episode), not content kind. Since channels are a separate endpoint/ID namespace and can be bookmarked/played through the same state, a channel and movie with the same numeric ID can unsave each other or replace history. A real colliding-ID pair was not obtained in this audit.
defects.recommended_correction: Use a stable kind:ID identity (plus episode ID for watch entries) consistently, migrate persisted state and test movie/channel records with equal IDs.

defects.title: Country-filtered movie/series pagination can stop on a filtered-empty server page
defects.description: catalog fetches a mixed country page and filters to the requested movie/serie kind locally. _PagedTitles treats an empty filtered result as the end. A mixed page containing only the opposite kind ends pagination even when later service pages contain matching records. The same end-on-no-fresh-items heuristic can truncate overlapping pages. No real upstream sparse-page fixture was executed.

evidence.symbol_or_behavior: mixed country page followed by kind filter

defects.recommended_correction: Expose raw-page continuation independently of visible items or continue fetching until a matching page/raw terminal page is reached, with a bounded cancellation-aware strategy. Test opposite-kind pages followed by matching pages.

defects.title: Several visible settings have no implementation consumers
defects.description: autoplay, externalPlayer, defaultQuality and dataSaver are defined, serialized and edited in Settings but never read by playback dispatch/source selection/artwork loading. UI changes are persisted successfully while the advertised behavior does not change.
defects.recommended_correction: Wire each preference into its actual operation with tests, or remove/disable it with an explicit limitation. Do not describe storage round-trip tests as feature behavior verification.

defects.title: Notification off preference does not disable notifications already permitted by OS
defects.description: Downloader configures running/completed/error/paused notifications unconditionally. The preference is used only to skip requesting the notification permission. If Android permission is already granted, setting the preference false still leaves the notification templates configured. The installed dependency configuration method confirms templates determine which task notifications are shown.
defects.recommended_correction: Apply enabled/disabled notification configuration on initialization and preference change, while explaining any OS-required foreground-service notification that cannot be disabled.

defects.title: Download pull-to-refresh is a no-op
defects.description: RefreshIndicator.onRefresh calls setState only and does not reload persistent records, check files or reconcile native state. It completes immediately without performing a refresh.

evidence.symbol_or_behavior: database reload only during one-time initialization

defects.recommended_correction: Add a service refresh/reconcile method and await it from pull-to-refresh; include empty-list refresh and missing-file tests.

defects.title: Release build uses debug signing configuration
defects.description: The release build type explicitly selects the debug signing configuration. Such an artifact is not appropriately signed for trusted production distribution; debug signing must not become the update/distribution trust identity. No signing key material was read or reproduced.
defects.recommended_correction: Use a separately managed release/upload signing identity outside source control and verify the final APK signer. Keep local debug-signed artifacts clearly labelled non-production.

defects.title: Brightness/volume controls start from fixed values and brightness is not restored
defects.description: The player initializes brightness=.6 and volume=.5 despite native getters being available, and never reads those getters. Window brightness is changed in MainActivity but player disposal does not restore system/default brightness, so adjustment can persist into normal app screens until activity recreation.
defects.recommended_correction: Read native state before displaying controls, preserve/restore original window brightness on exit, and keep system volume semantics explicit.

defects.title: Accepted imported settings can be outside DropdownButton choices
defects.description: AppSettings accepts any nonempty defaultQuality, playback speeds across .25–4, skipSeconds across 1–600 and arbitrary integer subtitle colors/backgrounds. SettingsPage supplies a much narrower fixed set and passes the imported value directly to DropdownButton. A schema-valid backup with speed 1.75 or skipSeconds 12 can trigger a Flutter dropdown assertion in debug and an invalid selected-state UI in release. Production crash behavior was not tested.
defects.recommended_correction: Normalize to supported option sets or render a valid custom option/fallback. Test Settings after imports containing accepted non-menu values.

defects.title: API refresh success message does not establish discovery success
defects.description: ApiService.initialize suppresses discovery HTTP/parse/allowlist/probe errors and returns normally. Settings then always reports Server discovery completed after awaiting it, even if configuration could not be loaded or accepted. Keeping a safe fallback is sound, but the UI does not distinguish fallback from successful refresh.
defects.recommended_correction: Return an explicit discovery outcome and show retained-default/failure/success status accurately without exposing sensitive request data.

defects.title: Application-wide cleartext media traffic is allowed
defects.description: Catalog API validation requires allowlisted HTTPS and disables redirects, which is positive. Separately, the Android app permits cleartext globally and media validation accepts arbitrary HTTP(S) hosts. HTTP media/artwork traffic can expose viewing requests and be modified on-path. This may be needed for legacy media compatibility, but is a documented trust/transport tradeoff, not secure end-to-end transport. No credential leak or active exploit was demonstrated.
defects.recommended_correction: Prefer HTTPS media/artwork where supported; narrow any necessary cleartext exceptions and document them. Do not bypass server auth/DRM or copy account credentials into media requests.

review_limitations: Source-only audit, not a penetration test or successful runtime/device proof. No critical-severity exploitable security issue was established. High-severity logic defects and debug release signing are blockers/risks called out explicitly.
A read-only snapshot can become stale if the parent implementation changes after report generation; use hashes and line references to re-review changed files.
Original platform/vendor-dependent behavior is mapped literally and differences are not silently marked complete.
No account credentials or shared constant values are reproduced, and no entitlement bypass was attempted.
